symptom: `call rest service post '…' (Body: $Payload)` sends the eight characters `$Payload` as the request body; `describe` prints `Body: template '$Payload'`. `check`, `exec` and `mx check` all pass — mx check only warns CW0094 "Variable 'Payload' is never used". The deprecated `body $Payload` clause, and a URL written as an expression (`@M.BaseUrl + '/rates'`, stored as that text so the request never reaches the server), behave the same
cause: `addRestCallAction` (mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_builder_calls.go) turned any non-string-literal URL or custom body into `fb.exprToString(...)` and stored that SOURCE TEXT as the Microflows$StringTemplate's Text, with no parameters. The grammar accepts `Body: <expression>` and `restCallUrl: expression`; the builder treated both as template text
file: `mdl/executor/rest_call_templates.go` (`restCallTemplate`, `checkRestCallTemplatesStmt` = MDL-REST05, `restCallAsTemplates`), called from `addRestCallAction`, `validate_microflow.go` (walkBody) and `flow_declared_match.go` (messageAsTemplate); tests `mdl/executor/cmd_microflows_rest_template_expression_test.go`; fixtures `mdl-examples/bug-tests/rest-call-1444-body-variable.mdl`, `rest-call-1444-expression-with-params.fail.mdl`
insight: Same rule `log`/`show message`/`validation feedback`/`send email` already applied (literal = template text, anything else = '{1}' with the expression as parameter) — the REST builder was the one template site that never got it, so grep for `exprToString(` assigned to a template's TEXT when auditing the class. The Studio Pro shape is measured, not assumed: ako/TestApp `Mappings.PostCustomRequestTemplate_2` (11.13.0) stores Text '{1}' + one TemplateParameter `$BodyPayload`, the shape the fix now writes (Text '{1}', Parameters marker 2 + one TemplateParameter). Fixing the builder alone is not enough: `create or modify` compares the declared AST with the AST parsed from describe, so `Body: $X` and the described `Body: template '{1}' with ({1} = $X)` must be normalized to one form there too, or every re-run sees a changed activity (the #905 rule). A string literal that spans lines arrives as a SourceExpr around the literal — unwrap it, or `Body: '<multi-line>' with (…)` is mistaken for an expression. Judge it at runtime with an echo server, not by the call's status: the baseline returned 200 with body `$Payload`; `on error continue` swallowed the failed URL request without a log line, so only the echo server's absent request showed it
